title: Sensex jumps 1,502 points as FMCG stocks lead the rebound
summary: The Sensex and Nifty recovered sharply on Wednesday, but the rally was much less convincing outside the large-cap indices.

sections.heading: A sharp recovery
sections.body: Indian shares bounced back on Wednesday, 25 November, after Monday's sell-off and Tuesday's market holiday. The Sensex closed at 83,938.28, up 1.82%, while the Nifty 50 gained 1.85% to finish at 25,819.25, according to Moneycontrol's closing report.

sections.heading: Consumer stocks take the lead
sections.body: FMCG and financial shares were among the strongest performers. Nippon India Mutual Fund's market note reported that Hindustan Unilever, Britannia and Tata Consumer Products were among the leading Nifty gainers. Metals, by contrast, came under pressure.

sections.heading: The broader market tells a different story
sections.body: Despite the jump in the benchmarks, more BSE-listed shares fell than rose, according to the same market note. Small-cap shares also ended lower. That is worth noting: Wednesday's rebound was concentrated in parts of the market rather than shared evenly across stocks.

sources.name: Nippon India Mutual Fund — Markets For You
